subject: physics
question_text: State the sign convention for heat (Q) and work (W) used in the first law of thermodynamics.

verification.note: Sourced from the Sri Chaitanya IPE Study Material for Jr. Students 2026-27 edition, physics volume, Chapter 12 Very Short Answer Question 4 (printed p.124). Only the question was taken; the answer, its steps and its mark split are original work — see docs/ORIGINALITY_MATHS.md. The 1 + 1 mark split is INVENTED and is a CLAIM until a Telangana IPE teacher confirms it. Physics hand-checked against NCERT Class-11 Chapter 12: heat Q is positive when supplied to the system and negative when taken out of it; work W is positive when done by the system and negative when done on it; with this convention the first law is written ΔQ = ΔU + ΔW.

recall_prompt: Say the steps you would write for this answer, in order. You can speak in English, in Telugu, or in both.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: Sign convention for Q
lines: Q is positive when heat is
Q is negative when heat is
steps.margin_note: First mark. Give both directions, in and out.
steps.why: Q and W enter the first law with opposite signs, so each needs its own separately stated direction rule.
common_mistakes: Giving only one direction for Q, in or out, and leaving out the other.
Reversing the sign, calling heat supplied TO the system negative.

recall.must_convey: That Q is positive when heat is supplied to the system and negative when heat is taken out of it.
accept: Q positive when heat supplied to the system
Q negative when heat leaves the system
reject: W positive when work is done by the system

steps.memory_tip: Q in, plus. Q out, minus.

steps.label: Sign convention for W
lines: W is positive when work is
W is negative when work is
steps.margin_note: Second mark. Give both directions for W, then the equation using this convention.
steps.why: A system that expands does positive work on its surroundings, so energy leaves through work when W is positive — the opposite direction to heat entering when Q is positive. That opposite sense is exactly why the first law subtracts W: ΔU = ΔQ − ΔW.
common_mistakes: Giving only one direction for W, by or on, and leaving out the other.
Mixing up W done BY the system with W done ON it.

recall.must_convey: That W is positive when work is done by the system and negative when work is done on it, and that the first law is written ΔQ equals ΔU plus ΔW with this convention.
accept: W positive when work done by the system
W negative when work done on the system
delta Q equals delta U plus delta W
reject: Q positive when heat supplied to the system

steps.memory_tip: W by the system is positive, W on the system is negative — the opposite sense to Q, where heat out is negative, and that is exactly why the first law reads ΔU = ΔQ − ΔW.

insider_note: State both signs for Q and both signs for W separately: heat in and heat out for Q, work by and work on the system for W.
